headline: Running streak hits a personal best at 20 weeks, with volume holding flat and a fresh lactate threshold marker anchoring current fitness.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Volume across the last four weeks sits at 127 km — essentially identical to the prior block's 125 km — confirming this is a consolidation phase rather than a drop. The consistency of that output across 18 runs over eight weeks is the more meaningful signal: you're sustaining a load that includes a 44 km long effort, two double-digit easy days back-to-back this week, and a 15.7 km threshold session, without accumulating excessive fatigue between blocks.

The July 2nd lactate threshold test at 4:24 /km and 178 bpm gives you a concrete current performance anchor. That pace sits clearly above your half marathon PB average (4:18 /km), which is the expected relationship, but it confirms threshold fitness is live and measurable — not inferred from old data. The two easy runs on June 30th and July 2nd (5:59 and 5:48 /km at 143 and 137 bpm respectively) look appropriately aerobic in context, and 137 bpm on a 13.77 km effort is a solid easy-day marker.

Strength is the one area where the data flags a mild dip: four sessions in the last four weeks versus what the prior block suggests. At 34 YTD sessions (1.3/week), the annual accumulation is still meaningful, but it's worth noting if the pattern continues another block.
watch_items: The easy-run HR drop (147 vs 157 bpm prior period) is a meaningful signal — watch whether this continues to trend down or stabilises over the next few long aerobic efforts.
Strength frequency has slipped to 4 sessions in the last four weeks; worth monitoring whether week 28 and 29 bring it back toward the 6-session prior-block rate.
The 20-week streak is a personal best — no action needed, but pay attention to how accumulated load feels across back-to-back days as you extend it further.
With threshold now benchmarked at 4:24 /km, watch how that figure moves over the next 4–6 weeks as the 30-day baseline accumulates more data points.
